newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish lira seen at 110,000 per dlr by year end.
newsitem.headline: Turkish lira seen at 110,000 per dlr by year end.

text.p: Turkish lira depreciation is expected to remain below inflation this year despite a sharp rise expected in the foreign trade deficit, Turkish bankers said on Monday.
But the higher trade deficit could create upward pressure on the lira next year, if not this year, they said.

"I think 110,000 lira will equal one dollar at the end of this year. The trade deficit is expected at around $20 billion, but it is hard to guess the market's reaction to this. Its negative effects may be seen throughout next year," assistant treasurer of a private bank said.
Bankers expect the Turkish lira to be in the range of 105,000 - 110,000 against the dollar at the end of 1996 if there are no major changes in dollar/mark parity.
Turkey's 1996 wholesale inflation target is 65 percent but economists predict it will overshoot. Inflation, measured by wholesale prices, was 79 percent in the year to August 1996.

Last year, the lira depreciated by 60 percent against the central bank's currency basket consisting of 60 percent marks and 40 percent dollars, compared to 1995 wholesale price inflation of about 65 percent.
Turkish trade and industry officials predict the foreign trade deficit will leap to $20 billion this year from $14.1 billion in 1995.
Lira depreciation has tracked wholesale inflation since end-1994 as part of Turkey's efforts to establish what is called a "realistic exchange rate" policy.

The lira lost 42 percent of its value against the currency basket in the first eight months of this year when wholesale prices rose by 52.7 percent. It fell by 44.2 percent to 86,200 against the dollar and 39.9 percent to 58,350 against the mark.

According to a trade weighted real exchange rate index prepared for Reuters by Faruk Selcuk, associate professor of economics at Bilkent University, the lira was overvalued by 2.2 percent in the first eight months in real terms.

The central bank tried to eliminate the overvaluation of the lira during the summer when inflation eased considerably and foreign currency earnings rose due to an influx of tourists and expatriate workers, bankers said.

The bank tried to prop up the dollar in the summer by using its daily dollar rate for banks' compulsory currency transfers, a key indicator for the domestic market. -- Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875.
